answer: Agents could admit newcomers through a rotating stake-and-audit mechanism: each identity locks scarce tokens, then a random trellis of existing agents checks its work against independent evidence before it can earn fees. A cipher-bound enrollment credential prevents one deposit from being reused across accounts, while the grove of auditors earns only when reviews agree with later outcomes. A sybil attacker must therefore lock more capital and risk slashing for each identity, rather than minting costless accounts.
